name: 2110 Prairie Avenue — the Harriet Rees house, a pale limestone front under a tall coped gable, its bow capped in copper below a five-arched loggia, the round-arched door at the head of a high stoop
aka: the Harriet F. Rees house (Cobb & Frost, 1888)

grade.why: Pictured: 11 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: Built in 1888 (Cobb & Frost, the register's row frontage-35-066), shown in the early-1890s street photograph and drawn on the 1911 sheet, which the T-1842 census rules present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The record claims the 1904 target to the sheet's date and no more; the house stood here until it was moved in November 2014.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the full-width front block on its south wall (lot frame u 37.7, v -3.75 from the middle of the rear lot line): the block's rear at the sheet's column 678, where the south wall steps in, and the south wall at row 1205, through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this copy. Rotation -0.682 degrees (the draft's) turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2110 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2110 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The full-width front block of the '3B' body, read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (the committed trace's affine fit, 0.186 m a pixel; docs/RESEARCH/k01-2110-rees-1922/README.md): 9.65 m from the column where the south wall steps in (678, lot u 37.7) to the stone front (column 730, lot u 47.35), and 7.8 m from the south wall (row 1205, lot v -3.75) to the north wall on the lot line with 2108 (row 1163.5, lot v 4.05). The rest of the body stands on K01's rear wings. The draft's largest rectangle had 20 x 6.25 m.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet over the main body: three storeys over a basement. The c. 1980s photograph shows them: the parlour storey and the one over it in the bow, and the third behind the five-arched loggia at the gable's foot.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the body pink (brick) and draws its street face in the blue of stone, the bow included; the early-1890s street photograph and the c. 1980s photograph both show a pale ashlar front.

principal_floor_m.note: The parlour floor about 1.8 m over the walk, at the head of a high stoop: the c. 1980s photograph shows a basement door under the stoop's landing with headroom, and the early-1890s photograph the landing's stone parapet standing about a man's height over the walk. Read as which storey a thing stands in, not measured.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, read as proportions of the c. 1980s photograph about the door (taken as 3.0 m to its crown): the parlour storey from the stoop's head to the bow's carved band, the upper storey from the band to the bow's copper cap, and the third from the cap to the gable's foot, where its loggia stands. The photograph looks up, so the upper heights are held to the lower ends of what it draws; the wall head stands at 12.7 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a stone front on its brick backing, as every K01 stone front (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the one K03 panel k03_brick lays (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

face_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the party walls and the rear are common brick, which no picture of 1904 shows: a Chicago common brick, salmon run (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

stone_front.note: Pale smooth ashlar in even courses, the bow standing on rock-faced base courses: the 2012 detail shows the smooth dressed stone of the gable and loggia, the c. 1980s photograph the rough stones under the bow, and the early-1890s photograph a pale front between 2112 and 2108. Bedford (Indiana) limestone for its buff-grey tone; the quarry is not read off any picture.

street_front_trim.note: The flat part of the front has one square-headed light in the upper storey, over the door, set plain in the ashlar (the c. 1980s photograph); the loggia's round heads are its own arches. T-3715: the loggia's six colonnettes, one beside each outer arch and one on each pier between, each a round shaft on a moulded base under a carved bell capital from which the arches spring (both later photographs, the 2012 detail close to): from the lights' sill (10.3 m) to their springing (11.65 m), engaged in the piers. The kit's foliate colonnette stands for them: its plinth, base and leafed bell are newly designed, not read stone by stone off the photographs' capitals, whose leaves are larger and looser (L-k01-2110-rees-3715). T-3716: the c. 1980s photograph's own camera (data/reference_views/rees_house_2110_prairie/aic_c1980s_front.json) reads the outer colonnettes at 1.63 and 5.93 m from the south corner, 0.86 m apart, where T-3715 had them at 1.15 and 6.05 (0.98 m): the loggia is 4.3 m across, not 4.9, its south end about 0.5 m further in. T-3716: both photographs show the colonnettes standing clear as round shafts, light between each shaft and the pier behind it, where T-3715 had them engaged with only their capitals showing: each now stands with its axis 0.11 m before the wall, the plinth's back on it (stand_m; the gap is reconstructed, L-k01-2110-rees-gable-3716).

wall_head.note: No cornice: the front runs up into its gable, which stands over the whole width from kneeler to kneeler (both photographs).

roof_form.note: The gable faces the avenue and the slated roof falls to the flanks behind it (the 2012 detail shows slates over the north flank behind the gable's rake). K01 builds it as a steep hip whose ridge runs on to the gable's back (T-3715, shaped_gable.roof_to_gable): the flanks are the true roof's slopes at the gable's pitch, hipped only at the rear (liberty L-k01-2110-rees-1922).

roof_pitch_deg.note: The flanks' slopes about 50 degrees: both later photographs draw the gable's rake near 50 degrees (the 2012 detail 49.5, the c. 1980s photograph 51), each looking up, which foreshortens a height a little; the draft had 52. The gable's own rake stands a little steeper than the slopes behind it, its coping clear of the slates.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a slate eave 0.3 m out over the flanks (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

roof_covering.note: Slate: the 2012 detail shows dark slates over the north flank behind the gable; the slate's quarry, the flashing and the ridge roll are reconstructed (L-k01-2110-rees-1922).

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K04's half-round copper gutter along the flanks' eaves, stopped at the gable, and one round copper pipe down the south wall near its rear corner to a splash stone; no picture shows the flanks (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

shaped_gable.note: The tall gable over the whole front, in the front's stone: its coped rakes from a kneeler at each corner to a carved finial at the apex, about 6.4 m over the wall head; one narrow light high in its face under the carved tympanum (both photographs). T-3714: the gable's head carved as both photographs show it, a carved field from a level base a little over the light's head (15.35 m) up into the apex, just inside the coping, and under it a carved drop over the light opening into two curled arms either side of it; the kit's stem, leaves and curls stand for the photographs' scrolled foliage (L-k01-2110-rees-carving-3714). The kneelers' corbels and the finial's leaves are left to T-3716's photo-match; the light is drawn round-headed and stands here segment-headed, the head the slab's kit cuts. T-3715: the slates run on to the gable's back (roof_to_gable), as both photographs show them beside the rake behind each kneeler, where the hip had fallen away a half-width short of it (L-k01-2110-rees-3715). T-3716: through both photographs' cameras (data/reference_views/rees_house_2110_prairie/) the light stands from about 13.3-13.45 m to 14.25-14.4 m and the carved field's base at about 15.0 m, where T-3714 had them at 14.0-14.95 and 15.35: both are lowered (the light's sill to 13.4 m, the field's base to 15.0 m), so the field is as deep as the photographs' and the light sits as far under it. Under each kneeler, at the front's corner, the c. 1980s photograph shows a carved corbel from about 10.3-10.5 m up to the gable's foot; K01's scroll console stands for it (bed 10.55 m, 0.5 m wide, a carved rosette in its roll), its carving the kit's, not read leaf by leaf (L-k01-2110-rees-3716). T-3716 (the gable's foot and kneelers): the c. 1980s photograph's front runs straight up into the gable, its ashlar unbroken over the loggia and nothing projecting across it, where K01's slab stood 0.32 m before the wall over the hip's street eave with a dark soffit under a ledge across the whole front: `flush` stands the slab's face 0.02 m before the wall's own, its base no wider than the front, and stops the hip's eave behind it, so the flanks' eaves end at the front's plane. Over the corners the photograph shows the rakes ending on short level kneeler stones over the carved corbels; at the south corner nothing stands over it, and at the north a plain pier, standing a little before the gable's face, rises from the corbel to a cap about 13 m up: `kneelers.ends` draws no pinnacle south and the north one as that pier (its height read through the photograph's camera, its depth before the face reconstructed, L-k01-2110-rees-gable-3716). The kneelers stand 3.72 m from the centre, over the corbels at the front's corners. T-3716 (the carved field): both photographs show the field filled edge to edge with scrolled foliage, where T-3714's stem and leaves ran as a narrow strip down its middle: `relief.fill_m` lays rows of the leaves' own scrolls every 0.22 m out to the panel's inner line beyond the leaves' reach, its carving the kit's, not read scroll by scroll (L-k01-2110-rees-gable-3716).

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K06 two-over-two double-hung sash in the square-headed lights, round-headed sash under a fanlight in the loggia's arches (L-k01-2110-rees-1922) T-3716: the loggia's lights stand at the far end of K06's reveal range (0.23 m back from the face, where the kit's is 0.115), since both later photographs show the glass well back in its arches, each arch a deep shadow round its sash; the depth is the kit's limit, not measured.

street_front_windows.note: North of the bow, one square-headed light in the upper storey over the door (the c. 1980s photograph; the early-1890s photograph shows the light over the door's arch); in the third storey the loggia's five round-arched lights in a row over the bow's cap, from about a sixth of the front's width in from its south corner to a quarter in from its north (both later photographs), 0.98 m apart. Their colonnettes and carved capitals stand on the piers between the lights and beside the outer two (street_front_trim.loggia, T-3715). T-3716: the loggia's lights re-read through the c. 1980s photograph's camera: 0.86 m apart (centres 2.06 to 5.5 m), each 0.6 m across between colonnettes about 0.26 m thick, where 0.98 m and 0.7 m had made the arcade 0.6 m too wide. T-3716: a carved band runs the loggia's width over its arch heads in both later photographs, scrolled foliage on a level stone from the outer colonnettes' capitals out; the kit's interlace on a dressed panel stands for it (carved_bands, a panel from 12.02 to 12.32 m, from s 1.42 to 6.14 m), its carving not read leaf by leaf and its bed laid just over the arches' crowns where the photographs' band dips between them (L-k01-2110-rees-gable-3716). `belts` names K01's own two string courses, unchanged, since a front with carved bands names them.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a landing 1.95 m deep, its front edge in line with the face of the parapet that carries it on south across the bow's foot, where the c. 1980s photograph shows that parapet's block standing as the stoop's south cheek begins to fall; the depth is chosen to that alignment, not measured (T-3715; L-k01-2110-rees-1922, L-k01-2110-rees-3715). It was the kit's 1.3 m.

stoop_width_m.note: A straight stoop about as wide as the door's arch between solid stone cheeks, square out from the door to the walk: the early-1890s photograph shows the cheeks ending in a pedestal at the walk and the c. 1980s photograph the treads running down toward the street.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the NORTH end of the front, north of the bow: the c. 1980s photograph (the viewer faces west, so right is north) shows the round-arched door between the bow and the north corner, and the early-1890s photograph an arched door between 2110's bow and 2108's front.

front_bays.note: The door's axis 6.45 m from the south wall, in the middle of the 2.65 m of flat front the bow leaves north of it (s 5.15-7.8).

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: no light in the main body's south wall, which stands 0.3 m off the lot line and about 0.75 m from 2112's north wall (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

north_bays.note: None: the north wall stands on the lot line against 2108 (the sheet's row 1163.5), built blank.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the main body's rear wall is covered by the rear body but for 1.45 m at its south end (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

rear_wings.note: The sheet's outline behind the full-width front block, read at full size through the trace's fit: the '3B' body runs on without a dividing line to column 612 (lot u 25.4), 1.45 m in from the south wall (row 1197-1199) to leave a light court, its north wall on the lot line to column 650 (lot u 32.5) and 1.15 m in from it behind; at its rear a small one-storey piece marked '1' (columns 586-610, rows 1170-1187). Three storeys on the sheet's one '3B'; their roofs are flat behind a fascia, which no picture shows (L-k01-2110-rees-1922).

sash_by_storey.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the flank and rear lights' sizes, as 2108's (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

basement_lights.note: RECONSTRUCTED: no basement light in the flat front: the stoop and its landing stand there (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

chimneys.note: A tall stack on the south flank just behind the gable, its head a little over the slopes behind the gable, under its apex (the c. 1980s photograph and the 2012 detail); the second, on the north wall at the rear, is reconstructed (L-k01-2110-rees-1922). T-3715: the south stack is laid in the front's pale stone to its cap, as both photographs show it against the gable; the rear stack stays brick, which no picture shows. T-3716: the south stack's head stands at 18.4 m, about 0.45 m over the kit's ridge + 0.6 (17.95 m): the c. 1980s photograph's camera puts its cap about 20 px over the render's, a little under half the finial's height below the apex.

entrance_kit.note: A round-arched doorway, the arch's crown about 3 m over the stoop's head, its transom under the arch (the c. 1980s photograph, where it bears the number 2110), in a moulded ring with no keystone of its own; the kit's keystone is laid near flush. The front yard to the 1904 street line, 7.3 m (lot u 47.35 to 54.65). T-3715: the landing carried south from the stoop across the bow's foot at the landing's height, past its crown to 1.5 m from the south corner,, faced to grade, behind a plain stone parapet whose top stands at the parlour lights' sills (the early-1890s photograph shows its level top under the bow's lights from the stoop to the bow's south end; the c. 1980s photograph its solid block beside the stoop's south cheek, the rest behind a shrub): as deep as the landing, 1.95 m out from the flat front, its back stepped round the bow's plan 0.12 m clear of its plinth, the parapet 0.5 m high and 0.25 m thick. Its depth before the bow's crown and its thickness are read as proportions, not measured (L-k01-2110-rees-3715).

boundary.note: An open walk before the house: the early-1890s photograph shows a carriage post at the curb before 2110 and no fence or wall at the walk.

yard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the 1904 yard as K14 conditions it, a flagged walk from the open front out to the stoop's foot, as wide as the stoop (L-k01-2110-rees-1922)

windows.why_not_ordinary: the parlour storey's three tall lights in the bow, each nearly from the stoop's height to the carved band, a transom light over each sash (the c. 1980s photograph, the early-1890s photograph's two in view); T-3716 reads them 1.15 m clear through the c. 1980s camera

the upper storey's three lights in the bow, as broad as the parlour's and shorter, under the copper cap (both later photographs); T-3716 reads them 1.15 m clear through the c. 1980s camera, the piers between them about 0.6 m

bays.note: The bow from grade to the third floor across the south part of the front, three lights a storey, its carved band at the upper floor and a copper cap under the loggia: the sheet draws it as a stone half-round at the south end of the front, and every picture shows it, the early-1890s photograph with its carved band. Its chord, 4.8 m from s 0.35 to 5.15, is read off the c. 1980s photograph as 0.62 of the front's width at the band, where the sheet's small symbol spans about 5.6 m; its rise, 1.5 m, between the photograph's turn of the side lights and the sheet's 2 m. T-3714: the carved band at the upper floor stands 0.45 m either side of the floor line, from a little over the parlour lights' heads to the upper lights' sills, as the c. 1980s photograph shows it, carrying K08's guilloche for the photograph's carved foliage; and the cap's moulded cornice is run in the cap's own copper, green with age in the 2012 detail (L-k01-2110-rees-carving-3714). T-3716: the c. 1980s photograph's camera reads the bow's centre lights about 1.26-1.33 m over their dark frames (1.15 m clear) where 0.95 m had been built, so the bow read as stone pierced by slots rather than as the photograph's three broad lights a storey on narrow piers; and each parlour light carries a transom light under its head (the photograph's bar about 0.55 m down), built as K06's transom sash.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling with a stone front and a rounded bay (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

the five round-arched lights of the loggia on colonettes at the gable's foot
the bow's three lights a storey, its carved band and its cap
the round-arched door at the north end with the light over it, and the high stoop
a stack on the south flank behind the gable
what_it_does_not_supply: any measure: no scale stands in it, and it looks up, which foreshortens heights
colour: it is black and white

a row of the same posts along the east curb opposite
a gas lamp on a post at the west curb further north
what_it_does_not_supply: the posts' sizes: no measure stands beside them
which east-side houses the row stands before: the picture's edge cuts them off
colour or stone: the photograph is sepia

what_it_supplies: the front's stone: pale, smooth, dressed ashlar in even courses
the gable's coped rakes, its carved tympanum, its narrow round-headed light and the kneelers' carved corbels
the loggia's five round arches on colonettes with carved capitals, under a carved band
the bow's cap: a copper cornice, green with age
slate on the flank behind the gable

the lower front, the flanks and the rear

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: T-1922 (the S12A package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2351) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits, its plan off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn read at full size, its front off the early-1890s street photograph of the 2100 block, which shows its bow, carved band, pale stone and stoop, and off two later photographs taken on this site before the house was moved in 2014 (c. 1980s, Ryerson & Burnham Archives; 2012, Glessner House Museum), read for forms only: a pale limestone front under a tall coped gable with a finial, a five-arched loggia at the gable's foot, a two-storey bow capped in copper at the south, and the round-arched door at the north at the head of a high stoop. The gable's carving, the loggia's colonnettes, the landing's parapet and the bow's carved band are T-1923's (T-3714, T-3715). The coach house shared with 2108 (mark_kimball_house_2108_prairie_coach_house) is T-1937's and is untouched. docs/RESEARCH/k01-2110-rees-1922/README.md.
